One-step real-MPS development smoke. No JSON target gain; prompt-only condition produced one arithmetic miss, while LoRA/random/zero retained 2/2 locality. Four questions, one family per role, no independent test.

studies.summary: The paired evaluator completed 1,216 CPU generations over 272 unique prompt strings in arithmetic and phrase/sentence tasks. This includes repeated development campaigns. One completion LoRA improved sentence agreement but regressed phrase completion and arithmetic locality; candidate quarantined. No promotion.

All seven fixed runs completed on direct Mac MPS. This repeats the already inspected pilot test families; JSON effects reproduced against random controls but retained locality regressions, concise gains remained small, and exact-instruction effects varied by seed. Hardware evidence only; no candidate promoted.

Corrected regrade of the same raw outputs. The first grader mislabeled explanatory responses with multiple integers; final-integer-token-v2 separates numeric correctness from strict formatting. Prompt-only improved this narrow development score; not a weight-edit result.

studies.summary: Four paraphrase surfaces per phrase or subject-verb family; family assignments are stratified by task type and kept inside one split. Includes a held-out confirmation pool not used in the development evaluation.

Prompt-only instruction strongly improved strict one-word output (11/104 to 99/104), while objective correctness was essentially tied. The task-stratified paired family interval included zero overall and by type. Small lexical and grammar probe set only; no weight edit. Its separate confirmation family was evaluated later and is now retired; see completion-confirmation-cpu-20261025.

A predeclared direct instruction sharply improved one-word formatting but reduced objective correctness overall on this finite family-held-out confirmation set. The subset intervals are wide; this does not establish a broad language ability or weight-edit effect. Retire this split.

Training command used only the validated train split and saved a conventional LoRA plus a layerwise norm-matched random edit. Loss decreased, but training completion does not establish behavioral usefulness.

The adapter gained on sentence-agreement development families against base, prompt and random controls but phrase-completion score fell. All target families are small and previously exposed development data; this is not independent confirmation.

A separate arithmetic development locality slice showed clear regression under the completion adapter, while norm-matched random stayed near base. The adapter was not evaluated on the retired completion confirmation set.

studies.adapter_training_source: completion v1 train split, seed 42, 64 updates, rank 4, alpha 8, q_proj/v_proj; frozen candidate from F014
studies.prompt_control_correction: Initial run used arithmetic-only system prompt due v2 not being recognized; original responses are preserved and excluded. Corrected prompt and repeated base were run post-hoc on the same spent holdout; base matched exactly 336/336.
studies.summary: A frozen v1 LoRA transferred strongly on new-vocabulary agreement sentences against base, corrected prompt and norm-matched random, but phrase completion dropped to 12/24 and an earlier arithmetic development locality test fell to 30/64. One small model, one adapter seed, post-hoc prompt correction and spent holdout; no promotion.

studies.hypothesis: Equal phrase and sentence sampling will improve phrase completion without damaging sentence generalization or arithmetic locality.
studies.summary: In one seed, task-balanced training saw 32 phrase examples versus 2 under uniform, but phrase development score was lower (14/24 versus 18/24); the direct family interval is wide and includes zero. Both adapters beat prompting on overall completion and neither showed a clear arithmetic regression on the small development locality slice. Fresh seed and fresh confirmation are required.

studies.hypothesis: A second seed will reproduce the sampler effects from F016 and show whether phrase completion improves when phrase exposure is increased.
studies.summary: Seed-44 adapters show sampler- and seed-sensitive development outcomes. Uniform scored 301/328 completion items (phrase 15/24, sentence 286/304); balanced scored 289/328 (phrase 13/24, sentence 276/304). The completion sampler contrast includes zero. On 64 arithmetic development items, uniform scored 38/64 while balanced scored 61/64; paired interval +26.6 to +46.9 points. This surprising locality result remains development-only and needs fresh arithmetic confirmation plus independent seed replication. Neither adapter is promoted; v2 confirmation is retired and untouched here.

studies.hypothesis: The seed-44 task-balanced adapter depends on particular projection and layer-half deltas for completion and arithmetic behavior.
studies.summary: Zeroing upper-half edits reduced sentence completion by 15.1 points and overall completion by 14.3 points relative to the full seed-44 adapter on previously exposed development cases. V-projection removal reduced completion modestly and arithmetic by 37.5 points. Arithmetic losses were measured on only 64 questions and do not establish broad capability loss. All evidence remains checkpoint-specific and development-only; do not transfer to Astra.

studies.hypothesis: The F017 seed-44 task-balanced completion LoRA arithmetic score will exceed base, task-matched prompt and norm-matched random on unseen confirmation families.
studies.development_reference: 61/64 arithmetic questions (95.3%) on previously inspected development families; confirmation score was 83.6%, a descriptive -11.7 points across different question sets.
studies.summary: On 32 preregistered hash-selected arithmetic confirmation families, the frozen adapter beat prompt, base and norm-matched random controls. Its 83.6% score was below the 95.3% arithmetic development score. This confirms one narrow signal while exposing development overestimation; it does not establish broader capabilities or phrase/sentence transfer. Do not tune on these selected families.

Fresh data infrastructure only. The phrase and long-distance agreement questions have deterministic answer keys and whole-family splits; sentence subjects and verb roots are disjoint across splits. No model has been evaluated on these v3 cases, so there is no behavior or edit result yet. Phrase confirmation includes only eight families and should be reported with wide uncertainty.

The edit beat base and the norm-matched random control on aggregate development completion, but did not establish an advantage over the explicit prompt. Phrase accuracy was below base. Post-hoc sentence analysis showed perfect plural-subject agreement and poor singular-subject agreement despite near-balanced sentence training updates. Treat as an exploratory edit-direction bias; do not promote or consume confirmation.

On the same already-inspected dev set, seed 43 repeats a strong plural preference despite a training sample with 21 singular and 11 plural subjects. Adapter-versus-prompt uncertainty includes zero and phrase accuracy is below base and prompt. This is a training-seed replication on old dev questions, not new generalization. Counts alone do not explain behavior; exact examples and optimization path also vary.

studies.intervention: Uniform sampling vs F021 task-balanced sampler at fixed seed and training settings
studies.comparator: F021 seed-42 task-balanced; 32 phrase and 32 sentence updates
studies.summary: Strong preregistered development result: uniform-sample adapter gains 26.2pp over prompt and 23.4pp over seed-42 task-balanced adapter, mostly by improving singular-subject sentences. Phrase performance remains below base. All test questions were already inspected; the samplers chose disjoint exact training samples. This shows the full training schedule can change behavior on this benchmark but does not isolate phrase frequency, generalize independently, show capability preservation or support transfer. Adapter remains quarantined; confirmation untouched.

studies.holdout_retirement: Completion confirmation families are retired from later candidate tuning once F024 responses are collected.
protocol_deviations: Evaluator progress output exposed base-arm correctness indicators for the first 325/432 completion cases before detection; no protocol or candidate changes followed.

Two zero-generation preflight failures were documented before retries: use of model alias instead of recorded local snapshot path for mixture; and use of archived adapter without its sibling run manifest for arithmetic. Retries used the same pinned model and checkpoint hashes.
studies.summary: Frozen uniform adapter independently confirms strong narrow sentence-completion gains over prompt, base and norm-matched random on 432 untouched questions, while phrase performance remains below base. It exceeds the fixed equal mixture by 4.9 points. On 312 fresh arithmetic questions it scores 99/312: above weak base/random (54/312) but below prompt (155/312) by 17.9 points. The candidate does not meet broad capability-preservation or promotion criteria. Retire both confirmation families; no later tuning on these cases.

training.data_factor_scope: The complete task exposure schedule, including deterministic update order, changes; update count is not isolated from order.

studies.conclusion: All six adapters beat the task-matched prompt on the previously inspected development set, but phrase accuracy stayed below base for every adapter. More phrase updates did not show a consistent dose-response across two seeds; sentence/task tradeoffs varied by seed. The fixed support set removes example-identity changes between ratios, but schedule order remains coupled to update allocation, sampling is with replacement, and only two seeds and seven phrase families are represented. No independent generalization, broad preservation, trait-map or Astra-transfer claim is supported.
